newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia needs $10.2 bln external funding 1997-2001.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia needs $10.2 bln external funding 1997-2001.

text.p: Tunisia on Tuesday told international donors it needed 11.2 billion dinars ($10.2 billion) to finance development projects for the period 1997 to 2001.

"The need for external financings is estimated to be 11.2 billion dinars," Prime Minister Hamed Karoui told some 40 representatives of the country's biggest foreign donors, including the World Bank and the European Union.
The meeting was called to look at financing for the 9th development plan 1997-2001 for which total domestic and foreign investments needs were put at 42 billion dinars.
Karoui said he expects that 20 percent of the foreign financing would come from foreign direct investment and 40 percent from grants and long term loans.
Bank loans and bonds will provide 40 percent from the international financial markets at an average 900 million dinars per year, he added.

To attract direct foreign investments, "it will be necessary to intensify action for the promotion of investment in Tunisia and reinforce the support given to foreign investors while ensuring the improvement of the business environment...," he said.

Grants and loans at concessional conditions would be essentially devoted to infrastructure projects, vocational training, protection of the environment, as well as the upgrading of the economy and the encouragement of private investment, he added.

"Our wish is that our partners support this effort..., thus contributing to the success of a flow of a development model with a human face, based on the interaction and complementarity between democracy, economic efficiency and social promotion," Karoui said.

International Cooperation and Foreign Investment Minister Mohamed Ghannouchi told the meeting that opportunities offered to foreign investors included the privatisation programme, the BOO (buy, own and operate) scheme for infrastructure and energy projects, and the opening up of the Tunis Stock Exchange.

He said a government programme set up last year to sell majority stakes in 62 public firms representing total net assets of 1.4 billion dinars was now implemented for one-third, and half of the assets will have been sold by the end of the year. ($=1.1 dinar)
